report_name: Bank of America Phishing Delivers ScreenConnect RAT via UAC Bypass

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The attack begins with a phishing email impersonating Bank of America, which contains a malicious link that leads to the download of a malicious installer.

attack_patterns.name: Match Legitimate Name or Location
attack_patterns.description: The malicious installer deploys the ScreenConnect remote access tool with the service name 'Windows Security' to blend in with legitimate system components and evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: Bypass User Account Control
attack_patterns.description: A VBScript payload modifies the installed service's security permissions using Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) strings, preventing it from being viewed or managed even with administrative privileges.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: The attackers used a legitimate version of ConnectWise ScreenConnect to gain full, persistent remote control over the victim's machine for command and control.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Service
attack_patterns.description: The malicious payload installs a new Windows service named 'Windows Security' to ensure the ScreenConnect tool runs persistently after system reboots.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
attack_patterns.description: A VBScript payload is executed by the installer to modify the security permissions of the newly created 'Windows Security' service, effectively hiding it.

tools.name: ConnectWise ScreenConnect
tools.description: A legitimate remote management and monitoring (RMM) tool that was deployed by attackers and disguised as 'Windows Security' to provide persistent remote access to victim machines.

tools.name: sc.exe
tools.description: The Windows Service Control utility was used with the 'sdset' command to modify the security descriptor of the malicious service, making it invisible to standard administrative tools.

campaigns.name: Bank of America ScreenConnect Phishing Campaign
campaigns.description: An ongoing phishing campaign observed in July 2026 that impersonates Bank of America to deliver a disguised version of the ScreenConnect remote access tool. The campaign uses a VBScript with SDDL strings to bypass UAC and establish persistent, stealthy access.

identities.name: Bank of America
identities.description: Impersonated in a phishing campaign to lure victims into downloading a malicious installer containing the ScreenConnect remote access tool.

infrastructure.name: ScreenConnect C2 Server
infrastructure.description: Attacker-controlled command-and-control server located in the United Arab Emirates, which the compromised ScreenConnect client connects to over TCP port 8041.

indicators.name: Hidden Service Creation via sc.exe sdset
indicators.pattern:
title: Hidden Service Creation via sc.exe sdset
id: 2b8c9a1d-4e5f-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of 'sc.exe sdset' to modify a service's security descriptor, a technique used to hide services from standard management tools.
references:
  - https://www.itsecurityguru.org/2026/08/04/fake-bank-of-america-phishing-emails-found-delivering-disguised-screenconnect-rat-via-uac-bypass/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1548.002
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' sdset '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of 'sc.exe sdset' to modify a service's security descriptor, a technique used in the Bank of America phishing campaign to hide the malicious ScreenConnect service.

indicators.name: Masqueraded ScreenConnect Service 'Windows Security'
indicators.pattern:
title: Masqueraded ScreenConnect Service 'Windows Security'
id: 8d3e4f5a-6b7c-4d8e-9f0a-1b2c3d4e5f6a
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a Windows service named 'Windows Security', a technique used to masquerade the ScreenConnect RAT.
references:

author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|endswith: '\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Windows Security'
    EventType: 'CreateKey'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a Windows service named 'Windows Security', which was used in a recent campaign to disguise a malicious ScreenConnect installation.

indicators.name: ScreenConnect C2 Traffic on Non-Standard Port 8041

title: ScreenConnect C2 Traffic on Non-Standard Port 8041
id: c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-1e2f-3a4b5c6d7e8f
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound network connections on TCP port 8041, which was used as a C2 channel for a malicious ScreenConnect client.
references:
  - https://www.itsecurityguru.org/2026/08/04/fake-bank-of-america-phishing-emails-found-delivering-disguised-screenconnect-rat-via-uac-bypass/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort: 8041
    Protocol: 'tcp'
    Initiated: true
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Monitors for outbound network traffic on TCP port 8041, the port used for command and control by the malicious ScreenConnect client in the Bank of America phishing campaign.
